knowledge_graph.title: Flurona
knowledge_graph.description: “Flurona” is a term coined in late 2020 by the Israeli Outbreak Management Advisory Team to describe the potential for contracting the flu and COVID-19 simultaneously. An unvaccinated teenager in Los Angeles was diagnosed with flurona on Wednesday, January 5, 2022.

related_questions.question: What is the meaning of Flurona?

text_blocks.snippet: "Flurona" is not an official medical term, but it refers to the simultaneous infection of an individual with both influenza (the flu) and SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19). It is not a new disease, but rather a coin termed to describe this dual infection.
snippet_highlighted_words: the simultaneous infection of an individual with both influenza (the flu) and SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19)

text_blocks.snippet: Essentially, "Flurona" is the colloquial term for someone experiencing symptoms of both the flu and COVID-19 at the same time. To determine if someone has "Flurona", they would need to test positive for both influenza and COVID-19.

text_blocks.snippet: "Flurona" is a non-medical term for the co-infection of COVID-19 and influenza (the flu) at the same time. It is not a new virus or disease, but rather a situation where a person is infected with both viruses simultaneously.

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms of flurona can include fever, cough, chills, sore throat, body aches, congestion, runny nose, and potentially vomiting and diarrhea. Some medical studies suggest that individuals with flurona may experience longer hospital stays or have an increased risk of death compared to those with either COVID-19 or the flu alone, but more research is needed to confirm these findings.
